topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: I always thought memories were like footprints in sand, eroding slowly, the deeper ones lasting longer. Running into Maria after all these years, I expected to see a flicker of recognition, a smile that mirrored the countless moments we shared. Instead, her eyes were ponds of unfamiliarity, stirring with polite interest. She laughed when I mentioned the treehouse by the creek, as if I’d spun a tale from a distant, mythical past. I found myself scrambling for common ground, each word feeling more forced than the last. It’s peculiar, the weight of silence when you’re the only one holding onto the past.
